READ CONTRACT shared by NXS-LOCAL-0159 and NXS-LOCAL-0160 (both build to it; neither changes it without a RELAY_QUESTION). GET /devices/{id}/inventory -> 200 {device_id, collected_at (ISO-8601, nullable when no run), job: JobView|null, contexts: [{context: string (\"physical\" or the VSID / vsys id), interfaces: [{name, parent (nullable), kind (physical|vlan|subinterface|loopback|bond|tunnel|other), state (up|down|unknown), addresses: [{address (with prefix), family (ipv4|ipv6), role (member|cluster_virtual)}]}], routes: [{destination, next_hop (nullable), interface (nullable), protocol (static|connected|default|ospf|bgp|rip|host|kernel|unknown), table (nullable)}]}]}. 404 {error: NOT_FOUND}. GET /clusters/{cluster_member_ref}/inventory -> 200 {cluster_member_ref, members: [{device_id, hostname (nullable)}], contexts: [{context, interfaces: [{name, kind, addresses: [...same as above...], presence: \"all\" | [device_id...], differences: [{device_id, field, value}]}], routes: [{destination, next_hop, interface, protocol, presence, differences}]}]}. Keys exactly as spelled, snake_case. The persistence model behind it (migration V13, additive): device_inventory_run(run_id PK, device_id FK devices, job_id, collected_at, context_count), device_interface(interface_id PK, run_id FK, context, name, parent, kind, state), device_interface_address(address_id PK, interface_id FK, address, family, role), device_route(route_id PK, run_id FK, context, destination, next_hop, interface, protocol, route_table). DeviceInventoryRepository (persistence module): recordRun(InventoryRun) writes one run with all children in one transaction; findLatestRun(deviceId) -> Optional<InventoryRun>; findLatestRuns(List<String> deviceIds). InventoryRun / InventoryContext / InventoryInterface / InventoryAddress / InventoryRoute are Java records in persistence.device.inventory with exactly the fields above.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
Every public type names the clause it implements (14C D-n, 13F section n, C2/C4 section n).
Do NOT use './ui2/gradlew -p ui2 build' without '-x :integration-tests:test'. Do not run the full Python pytest suite. Eleven Gradle subprojects.

No address, hostname, serial, credential or raw command output reaches a log line, an exception message, an audit row or a stored column beyond the columns 14C D-4 names. Fixtures use RFC 5737 / RFC 3849 documentation addresses only.
If a contract clause and this packet disagree, raise a RELAY_QUESTION and STOP; never reconcile silently and never relax a direction test.
No emoji, no tool-identifying footer, no external URL in commits, the PR or code comments.
Commit early and often. Open the PR at the end; do not merge. The PR body carries a summary and a test plan only.
Coordinate with 0159 only through the shared contract text and its pushed lane; do not edit files under ui2/persistence or ui2/worker.
The SESSION_CLOSE names the routes with status codes, the merger class and its rules, the frontend components, and the test counts before and after.

in: Service read model: InventoryQueryService (latest run per device -> the device inventory shape; unknown device 404; device without a run -> 200 with collected_at null and empty contexts) and ClusterInventoryMerger (pure function: list of member device ids + their latest runs -> the cluster shape; join interfaces by (context, name) and routes by (context, destination, next_hop, interface); presence 'all' when every member has the row, else the list of device ids that have it; differences list per field whose value differs across members; cluster_virtual addresses collected once on the cluster row, member addresses left under members; deterministic ordering). Unit tests for the merger: identical members, one member missing a route, differing interface state, VIP appears once, two contexts.

Routes on DeviceRegistrationController or a new InventoryController: GET /devices/{id}/inventory, GET /clusters/{cluster_member_ref}/inventory (404 when no device carries that ref), POST /devices/{id}/inventory/collect -> admits the vendor's inventory capability with idempotency key deviceId + ':inventory:' + a per-request nonce the client sends (or the minute bucket if absent), returns 202 {job_id}; 409 ADMISSION_REFUSED on refusal; gated by a new ActionRegistry action id for collection (write class) and the existing read gating for GETs; register the wildcard route keys. JSON keys exactly as the shared contract spells them.

Frontend: adminApi.ts types (DeviceInventory, ClusterInventory, the nested records) and calls getDeviceInventory, getClusterInventory, requestInventoryCollect; InventoryScreen detail: replace the placeholder panels with InterfacesPanel (table: name, kind, state, addresses with a small role chip for cluster virtual), RoutesPanel (destination, next hop, interface, protocol chip, table), per-context tabs when more than one context; cluster row detail uses the cluster inventory with a member-difference marker (chip naming the members) and VIPs on the cluster row; a 'Collect now' button calling requestInventoryCollect and polling the device until the job is terminal (reuse the AddDeviceDialog polling pattern); empty and error states kept. No role-conditional rendering (architecture test). vitest coverage for the merger-fed cluster view, the panels and the collect button.
Tests: service unit tests for InventoryQueryService and the controller (fakes), merger tests, frontend tests; architecture tests untouched and green.
out: Persistence types, migration, parsers, executor (0159); any live device contact; configuration screens; scheduler; changing the shared contract without a RELAY_QUESTION.

completed: GET /devices/{id}/inventory and GET /clusters/{cluster_member_ref}/inventory (InventoryController, InventoryQueryService) exactly per the shared READ CONTRACT: device shape with collected_at null / empty contexts pre-collection, 404 NOT_FOUND for an unknown device_id or an unowned cluster_member_ref.

ClusterInventoryMerger: a pure static merge over (member ids in order, latest InventoryRun per id) -> merged contexts, joining interfaces by (context, name) and routes by (context, destination, next_hop, interface), computing presence (All | Members) and per-field differences against a first-member baseline, folding only cluster_virtual addresses onto the merged row de-duplicated by (address, family) -- an identical VIP reported by every member appears exactly once, member addresses never copied onto the cluster row.

POST /devices/{id}/inventory/collect (InventoryCollectService): admits the vendor's inventory capability through a dedicated inventoryJobAdmissionService/inventoryCapabilityRegistry pair (cp_inventory_collect / pan_inventory_collect placeholders, InventoryCapabilityIds), idempotency key deviceId + ':inventory:' + client nonce or a UTC minute bucket, 202 {job_id} on admission/dedup, 409 ADMISSION_REFUSED otherwise; gated by a new device_inventory_collect ActionRegistry action (role:onboarding_admin, write class).

GateChainInterceptor's wildcard route fallback generalized from 'last segment only' to 'the first interior segment (tried right to left) whose wildcarding resolves' so the id/ref in the middle of these three new routes still gates; the pre-existing single-segment routes (GET /devices/*) resolve identically on their first attempt -- proven directly by the new GateChainInterceptorRouteResolutionTest since GateChain has no cheap test double.

InventoryScreen.tsx: device rows are now selectable; a selection mounts InventoryPanels.DeviceInventoryPanels (key={device_id}, remounted per selection so useFetchOnMount's own mount effect re-runs on a changed fetcher); no selection keeps the original static empty-state tabs verbatim (existing InventoryScreen.test.tsx scenarios untouched, still green).

InventoryPanels.tsx: InterfacesPanel/RoutesPanel (per-device, tabbed by context when more than one), ClusterInterfacesPanel/ClusterRoutesPanel (presence + differences columns), ClusterMembersMarker (a chip naming each member), CollectNowButton (submits then polls GET /devices/{id} until its job is terminal -- the same cancellable-interval pattern AddDeviceDialog already uses), DeviceInventoryPanels (the composed detail view).

GateChainInterceptor is a security-critical, shared file with no prior dedicated unit test; this movement both changed its wildcard-matching algorithm and added the first such test (GateChainInterceptorRouteResolutionTest, reflection-based). Flagged for extra reviewer attention given its role in AC-4's gate chain, even though the full architecture-tests and service-test suites pass and the change is backward-compatible by construction (last-segment wildcarding is tried first, matching the prior behavior exactly).

The 'protocol'/'kind'/'state' baseline in ClusterInventoryMerger is the first cluster member (in caller order, which the service sorts by device_id) that carries the row -- not a majority vote. Documented in the class's own javadoc; flagged here since 14C/13F do not spell out a tie-break rule explicitly and this is the interpretation this movement chose.
